title: SE Ranking study of 50,807 health searches and 465,823 AI Overview citations (Germany)
subject: How Google AI Overviews select the URLs they cite

provenance.primary_study: SE Ranking — analysis of 50,807 health-related searches and 465,823 citations in the German market. Prompted by a Guardian article, 'Google AI Overviews put people at risk of harm with misleading health advice'.
provenance.what_we_actually_hold: A secondhand summary: an X/Twitter thread by Alex Groberman (@alexgroberman, Jan 2026), archived at source-thread-groberman-x.md, plus one chart image from SE Ranking archived at chart-trusted-medical-vs-general-sources.png.
provenance.reliability: UNVERIFIED SECONDHAND. The primary SE Ranking report has not been read. The relaying author sells SEO packages and the thread interleaves study numbers with promotion for his own products; the promotional claims are excluded from `study_findings` below and kept separately in `authors_commentary`.
provenance.rule: These numbers must NOT be written into brain/state.yaml or brain/thesis.md as measured facts. They are a prior about AI-answer behaviour, not a measurement of FMD (GATE-4). Treat as hypothesis-generating only.

ai_overview_trigger_rate_percent.note: more than 82% of health-related searches triggered an AI Overview

cited_url_organic_overlap_percent.implication_as_stated: roughly 26% of AI-cited URLs sit outside the organic top 100 entirely; even when AI and organic cite the same domain they often cite different URLs

authority_beats_expertise.claim: Domain authority often outweighs expertise in AI Overviews.
authority_beats_expertise.evidence_cited: One of the top five most-cited domains was a career/job platform, not a hospital, government site, or academic journal.

youtube.claim: YouTube was the leading source for health-related AI Overviews while ranking 11th in organic results for the same queries.
youtube.quoted: This shows that AI often prioritizes video content even when more authoritative, easier-to-find sources exist.

stated_pattern: government and academic sources are underrepresented
authority-heavy but non-expert sites show up
scale and consistency matter more than pedigree

authors_commentary.note: The author's inferences and product pitches, kept separate from the study's numbers.
inferences: AI Overviews infer trust from authority signals plus parseability rather than credentials.
Ranking a page is no longer sufficient; publishing the page AI wants to quote (comparison, FAQ, definition, buyer guide, explainer) is a separate job.
'Operational authority' is buildable by ordinary businesses: quotable pages, coverage at scale, authority signals to break ties.
unrelated_claims_in_the_same_thread: 64% of the SaaS blogs in a separate study grew search traffic in 2025
an ecommerce customer grew search traffic 126%
a recommendation of '3 DR50+ backlinks from domains LLMs already trust'
authors_commentary.commercial_interest: Thread repeatedly links seo-stuff.com Gold Plan and Premium Content Bundle. Discount accordingly.

converges_with_measured_evidence: The Semrush Brand Performance export (2026-07-19) measures freshmobiledetail.com at 0 citations while the brand is mentioned 8 times — every citation FMD earns comes from a third-party property (trustindex.io 11, reddit.com 8, itsawash.net 8, zayasmobiledetailing.com 7). The study's 'AI cites what is quotable and authoritative, not what ranks' pattern is the same shape.

The study's finding that only 36% of AI-cited URLs sit in the organic top 10 is consistent with FMD's split state: 0 organic top-10 positions across 479 tracked keywords, yet 8 ChatGPT mentions at an average position of 1.75 when mentioned.
does_not_change: GATE-1 stays closed. The study's 'coverage at scale' advice is exactly the instruction the gate exists to refuse: 14 pages are already discovered-and-not-indexed. Publishing more pages does not become correct because a third-party study likes volume.
T1 (entity trust is step zero) is unaffected — if anything the study's 'authority breaks ties' finding reinforces it.
relevance_to_fmd.open_question_it_raises: Whether a small number of genuinely quotable, answer-shaped assets (definitions, comparison tables, structured FAQ) on already-indexed URLs would earn citations without adding new pages. That is a refresh/consolidation question on existing pages, not a publishing question, so it is not gated by GATE-1.
